root_cause.text: The TCP-AO inbound MAC verification in `net/ipv4/tcp_ao.c` used սովորական `memcmp()` to compare the computed MAC against the packet MAC, causing an early-exit, non-constant-time comparison that could leak timing information.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `if (memcmp(phash, hash_buf, maclen))` with `if (crypto_memneq(phash, hash_buf, maclen))` and adds `select CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS`/`#include <crypto/utils.h>`, while the CVE says the fix is to “compare [MACs] in constant time” to prevent timing attacks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make TCP_AO select the crypto utility library it depends on.
intent_record.what: In the Kconfig entry for `TCP_AO`, a new dependency selection was added: `select CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS`. The rest of the option definition remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: Enabling `TCP_AO` now also pulls in the `CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS` library automatically at build time, ensuring required crypto helper functionality is available when TCP Authentication Option support is configured.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the missing crypto utils header needed by this TCP code.
intent_record.what: A new include directive was added: `#include <crypto/utils.h>` alongside the existing TCP-related headers.
intent_record.how: This makes declarations or helper macros from `crypto/utils.h` available in this compilation unit, enabling the file to use crypto utility functions or types that were previously unavailable at compile time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use constant-time comparison for TCP-AO hash verification to avoid timing-sensitive MAC checks.
intent_record.what: In tcp_ao_verify_hash(), the MAC comparison changed from memcmp(phash, hash_buf, maclen) to crypto_memneq(phash, hash_buf, maclen).
intent_record.how: The function now performs a constant-time byte comparison for the TCP-AO authentication hash, avoiding data-dependent timing behavior during MAC verification while preserving the same success/failure outcome.

grouping_result.intent: Make TCP_AO select the crypto utility library it depends on.
Add the missing crypto utils header needed by this TCP code.
Use constant-time comparison for TCP-AO hash verification to avoid timing-sensitive MAC checks.

relevance_review.reason: The change is about selecting the crypto utility library dependency for TCP_AO, not about fixing the MAC comparison logic in tcp_ao.c or replacing non-constant-time memcmp() with a constant-time comparison.
The change only adds a missing crypto utils header and does not address the TCP-AO MAC comparison issue caused by using memcmp() instead of a constant-time comparison.
The group directly addresses the reported root cause by replacing the non-constant-time MAC comparison in TCP-AO verification with a constant-time check, mitigating the timing leak.

candidates.rationale: This is the timing-sensitive MAC verification statement. Using memcmp() on attacker-influenced packet MAC bytes can exit early on mismatch, leaking information through timing and causing the vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the inbound TCP-AO MAC verification check. Using memcmp() here performs an early-exit comparison against attacker-influenced packet MAC bytes, which is not constant-time and can leak timing information.
